editorial:
You follow Henry Barthes, a substitute teacher who drifts between schools and keeps everyone at arm's length. The film drops you into a rough high school where teachers are burned out, students are hurting, and nobody seems to have answers. It feels heavy and honest, with a quiet sadness running through every scene. Henry tries to help, but his own walls make it hard to connect. You watch him bounce between classrooms, home life, and a young runaway he takes in, while the school around him keeps breaking down. It is not a feel-good story, but it pulls you in with real people and raw emotions.

The acting is strong, especially Adrien Brody as Henry, and the supporting cast makes the school feel alive. The pacing is slow and moody, so if you want action or laughs, this may not be for you. Some scenes hit hard, and the film does not offer easy comfort. Still, if you like serious dramas about people trying to care in broken systems, it is worth your time. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: Henry finally lets his guard down and tries to protect Erica, the runaway he has been sheltering, but the system and his own pain catch up with him. The school keeps falling apart, and a student tragedy pushes everyone to the edge. In the end, Henry does not fix the school or save everyone. Instead, he accepts that caring still matters, even when it hurts, and he keeps moving forward with a little more openness than before.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves serious character dramas and school stories.
